column1: # PanicOS tool manifest: the single source of truth for bundled tools.
# The build installs every package named here. Inside the image,
# panicos-selftest checks that each binary is on PATH and, when a smoke command
# is given, that it exits 0. Packages that ship no binary (firmware, kernel)
# Smoke commands run under `bash -c` with no terminal and no stdin. Prefer one
# that makes the tool do real work over one that only prints a version.
# --- Getting recovered data off the machine ----------------------------------

column3: d=$(mktemp -d) && printf 'int main(void){return 0;}' | gcc -x c -o "$d/smoke" - && "$d/smoke"; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s
d=$(mktemp -d) && printf 'int main(){return 0;}' | g++ -x c++ -o "$d/smoke" - && "$d/smoke"; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s
d=$(mktemp -d) && python3 -m venv "$d/venv" && "$d/venv/bin/pip" --version; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s
d=$(mktemp -d) && printf 'fn main() {}' > "$d/smoke.rs" && rustc -o "$d/smoke" "$d/smoke.rs" && "$d/smoke"; s=$?; rm -rf "$d"; exit $s
